intro.title: Explore Queen's Park Savannah
intro.description:
As the 'green lung' of Port of Spain, Queen's Park Savannah is more than just a park—it's a microcosm of the Trinidadian lifestyle. From local residents jogging in the early morning to the lively food vendors at night, and the costumed dancers during Carnival, this place beats with the most passionate pulse of the Caribbean.

Formerly the St. Clair Estate, it was purchased by the Town Council from the Peschier family in 1817 and retained as a public recreation ground. Today, with a perimeter of about 3.5 kilometers (2.2 miles), the one-way road surrounding it effectively forms the world's largest traffic roundabout.

visitGuide.title: Visiting Tips
items: 🌞 Morning Energy Tour: Jogging ➔ Visit the Royal Botanic Gardens to the north ➔ Drink fresh coconut water
🌙 Evening Culture Tour: Architectural photography ➔ Enjoy the sunset ➔ Taste local street food at the southern night market
🎉 Festival Experience: If possible, visit during Carnival (usually February or March)

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: 🔄 World's Largest Roundabout: A 3.5km one-way perimeter road, a paradise for joggers and fitness enthusiasts.
🏰 The Magnificent Seven: Seven famous Victorian-era colonial buildings line the western side of the park, perfect for photography.
🎭 Carnival Epicenter: The main stage for the world-famous Trinidad Carnival, hosting various cultural events year-round.
🍢 Night Market Food: Taste local street food (like Doubles, Bake and Shark, Corn Soup) at the southern stalls after sunset.

route.title: Tour Route
route.overview: The ideal route to explore Queen's Park Savannah:
steps: Start your morning exploring the Royal Botanic Gardens and Emperor Valley Zoo on the north side.
Stroll along the western edge to admire and photograph the famous 'Magnificent Seven'.
Relax on the vast lawns and grab a fresh coconut water from a local vendor.
After sunset, head to the food stalls on the southern end for authentic Trinidadian street food.
supplements: Parking around the perimeter can be difficult during holidays; taking a taxi is recommended.
Expect major road closures and crowds during Carnival season; plan ahead.
When trying street food, don't forget to sample the local slightly spicy sauces.

knowledge.title: Discover the Charm of Queen's Park Savannah

sections.title: Historical Evolution
sections.content: Formerly the St. Clair sugar estate, the Town Council bought the land in 1817 as a green space, witnessing Port of Spain's growth from the colonial era to a modern city.

sections.title: World's Largest Roundabout
sections.content: Covering about 260 acres, the Savannah is encircled by a 3.5-kilometer one-way road, considered the largest traffic roundabout in the world.

sections.title: Soul of Caribbean Carnival
sections.content: This is the epicenter of one of the world's largest carnivals—Trinidad Carnival. The Grand Stand has witnessed countless calypso competitions and parade of the bands.

hours.title: Opening Hours & Visitor Info
hours.summerTime: Mornings for exercise, evenings for night market food
hours.winterTime: Magnificent Seven, Night Market, Carnival Grand Stand
hours.warningTime: You must visit the food strip on the southern side after sunset. Try Doubles and corn soup—it's the ultimate Trinidadian culinary experience!
hours.tip: The western walkway offers the best vantage point for photographing the famous 'Magnificent Seven'.

transport.title: Transportation
transport.airportDesc: From Piarco International Airport, a taxi ride to downtown Port of Spain takes about 40-50 minutes.
transport.selfDriveDesc: The road around the park is a massive one-way roundabout (counter-clockwise). Please observe traffic signs and speed limits.
transport.busDesc: Most public transport and maxi-taxis in Port of Spain pass by or near the Savannah, making it highly accessible.
transport.intercityDesc: The park has a flat 3.5-kilometer perimeter, perfect for walking or jogging a full lap.
transport.cyclingDesc: Rideshares or local taxis are very convenient options.
transport.tipsDesc: Since it's the world's largest roundabout, if you miss your turn, you might have to drive the entire 3.5km loop again!

items.name: John Mitchell
items.text: The largest roundabout in the world! Eating Doubles here at night was my best experience in Trinidad.

items.name: Maria Santos
items.text: Amazing open space with so much history. The Magnificent Seven on the west side are a must-see. A Port of Spain essential.

items.name: David Thompson
items.text: Jogging here every morning feels great. Grabbing a fresh coconut water is the perfect way to start the day.

items.name: Sarah Williams
items.text: During Carnival, this is absolutely the center of the world! The atmosphere is insane, and the Grand Stand shows are unforgettable.

items.name: Michael Roberts
items.text: Great place to experience local life. The corn soup and Bake and Shark at the night market are delicious.

items.name: Lisa Richardson
items.text: Beautiful park, with the Royal Botanic Gardens right to the north. Fantastic scenery and a perfect spot for photos.

items.name: Kevin James
items.text: Huge space, lots of families playing cricket here on weekends. The traffic around is busy, but it's peaceful inside the park.

items.name: Jennifer Lewis
items.text: The crown jewel of Port of Spain. Not just a green space, but the best place to understand Trinidad's culture, history, and food.

historyTimeline.title: Historical Timeline

items.title: Early Period: Park Establishment
items.description: Queen's Park Savannah was established as a public recreational space for the citizens of Port of Spain, and has long been regarded as an important gathering place by locals.

items.title: 20th Century: Facility Improvement
items.description: With the development of Port of Spain, the Savannah gradually improved its facilities, becoming an important place for citizens' leisure and cultural events.

items.title: 21st Century: Cultural Landmark
items.description: Entering the 21st century, with its beautiful environment and convenient location, it has attracted more visitors and become an iconic cultural space in Port of Spain.

historyTimeline.guideContent: When visiting, you can enter the Savannah from Queen's Park East; then walk around the perimeter and enjoy the scenery and leisure atmosphere; if you have enough time, you can relax in the green spaces and experience the local culture. Finally, explore the surrounding areas of Port of Spain and feel the charm of Trinidad and Tobago's capital.

officialManagement.title: About Queen's Park Savannah
officialManagement.text: Queen's Park Savannah is a famous public park in Port of Spain, featuring beautiful green landscapes and rich cultural value. It is managed and maintained by the relevant authorities of Trinidad and Tobago.
